## ACCEPT — objectui#8334 / PR #9193

Reviewed against the diff at `cfdc50f1627b835e66da2667ef5f209bae4c8797`, not against the report.

**Provenance check first** (the act that exists because a report once described a commit the PR did not carry): `git ls-remote` = `cfdc50f16…`, PR `head.sha` = `cfdc50f16…`, and the diff against the merge-base reads `2 files changed, 394 insertions(+), 24 deletions(-)` — matching the PR's own `additions`/`deletions`/`changed_files` exactly. One commit, one tree, no gap.

### 0. The corrections, and one of them is to my dispatch

**⭐ My starred direction-B hypothesis was false, and the dev killed it with a measurement rather than an argument.** I wrote that the `json` fence growth in `content/docs/components` (4 → 8 on my reading) might mean some of the five named plaintext blocks had already been retagged — i.e. that direction B was partly underway. It is not: the growth is in `icon` / `data-table` / `combobox` / `index` / `box`, none of them one of the five, and PR objectui#8324's merged diff only *added* a ```` ```json ```` fence, with its two deletions being blank lines. The hypothesis was a plausible story built on two numbers and no causal read, and it would have sent the round looking for work already done.

**⭐ And a second one, which I think is the more useful of the two: I verified the card's premises inside the card's frame without asking whether the frame was right.** I re-measured "the corpus is currently clean" per file across the five pages and reported ✅ Holds. It does hold — of those five files. It is false of the **class**, and the class is what the card is about. I checked the numbers and inherited the scope, which is the same shape as generalising from a sample to a member I never opened. ⛔ A premise re-derived within a scope nobody re-derived is not re-derived.

I independently confirmed the instance that makes the point, on `origin/main`:

```
content/docs/guide/architecture.md
  ```tsx
  { type: 'text', content: 'Hello, ${user.name}!' }
```

An expression on a typed node, in an unscanned fence, today. Neither judged nor reported. It is carried, so it is not a finding — but it is proof the shape is live rather than theoretical, which is precisely what the card's "not urgent" rested on not being true.

**The population.** My own directional read: **27 files** under `content/docs/fields` match `^\s*type: '` (control with a known direction: the same predicate with a nonsense key returns **0**). ⛔ That is a *file* count under a text predicate — a floor, and it does not separate object-literal bodies from TS `interface` bodies. It is not the dev's 26 and is not offered as a competing number; it is an independent reading that the class is very much larger than five and that the card's five was a `content/docs/components`-scoped figure. The instrument's own count is the one that decides.

### 1. What I verified in the diff

| claim | how | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| ⛔ **`plaintext` is not admitted** | `JSON_FENCE_LANGUAGES = ['json', 'jsonc']` — the line is unchanged; and it is pinned `not.toContain('plaintext')` with the PR objectui#8324 rejection quoted in the failure message | ✅ mechanism **and** pin |
| ⛔ **the judged population is not widened** — triage's binding fence | every call site of `parseFenceDialect` read: one at the blind-spot leg, **inside `if (!fence.scanned)` and before its `continue`**, one in the in-run control. The judged path (`inventory.push`, `bump`, the `counters`) is not reachable from the new code | ✅ structural, not promised — this is the leg I would have rejected the PR over |
| the fence is pinned, not just honoured | a separate test asserts the judged language set EQUALS `JSON_FENCE_LANGUAGES` and that every blind-spot fence is **not** in it — disjointness by construction | ✅ the fence becomes a red test if a later change crosses it |
| **the gate stays report-only** | ⛔ the diff touches **no** `process.exit` / `exitCode` line at all — verified by grepping the diff itself, not the file | ✅ 26 reported fences cannot redden `Build Docs` |
| **the replacement pin is a floor, per file** | five per-file `toBeGreaterThan(0)` assertions plus a `>= 5` non-vacuity floor, and ⛔ **no equality on the total** — with a comment saying why an equality would make a report-only gate blocking through the back door | ✅ and the per-file failure message tells the next reader what to do if a page was legitimately retagged, ⛔ including "do NOT delete the list" |
| the in-run control is two-sided | positive fixture must normalize **and** yield exactly `[filter-ui, text]`; negative fixture (an interface body) must not parse | ✅ per counter, both directions |

**NOT MEASURED by me:** the byte-identical census output, the 26/18/3 split, the two ablation legs, and every gate verdict. Bare checkout, no `node_modules`, and the gate loads a carriage table — ⛔ I will not write a leg I cannot execute. The structural reads above are what substitute for the reachability half of the byte-identity claim; the rest is CI's to confirm.

### 2. Why this is accepted rather than sent back

Three things, in order.

**The pin was part of the defect, and the dev found that without being told.** `expect(census.unscannedJsonLike).toEqual([])` passed *because the leg it pinned was blind* — a test whose green was produced by the very failure it existed to catch. And its failure message instructed the next reader to *"Widen `JSON_FENCE_LANGUAGES` deliberately"*, which is the one fix content rejected on PR objectui#8324. ⛔ That message would have walked the next person straight into the blind spot the gate exists to close. Correcting the prose alongside the code is the right call and it is the second time today a round has made it.

**Direction A was chosen on measurement, and the measurement is what rules out B and C** — not taste, and not the fence. Against a 26-block class, B is a twelve-page teaching-content rewrite and C is a 26-entry hand-maintained list that still leaves the instrument blind and merely *asserts* `none`. Only A makes the coverage line **derived**. The card offered three options sized against a population that does not exist, and the round said so instead of picking the one that looked cheapest.

**The normalizer is two removals of dialect, not a heuristic.** The card sketched "an object literal whose first key is `type`, say" — which would have been a guess wearing a detector's clothes. What landed re-spells single-quoted strings and quotes bare identifiers **in member position** (the same positional predicate `dropElisionStrings` already uses), is comment-aware so an apostrophe in `// don't` cannot corrupt the rest of the body, can invent no member, and is a pinned no-op on strict JSON. Then it asks **the identical existing `collectNodes` question** of both spellings. That is a dialect normalization, ⛔ not a pattern for the shape someone expected to find.

⭐ And the note I most want kept: **the dialect controls still passed under ablation leg 1.** They exercise `parseFenceDialect` directly while leg 1 severs its wiring into `analyze`. The controls catch a broken normalizer; the per-file corpus floor catches a disconnected one. ⛔ Two guards that look redundant on the page are not — and the round reported that rather than presenting three green legs as three confirmations.

### 3. Routed, ⛔ not folded in

**objectui#9194**, filed bare: the shared doc-fence scanner's `/^\s*```(\S*)\s*$/` reads a four-backtick opener as a three-backtick fence in a language named `` `markdown ``, inverting the nesting so the inner block reads as prose. Two gates share the predicate; one corpus site today. Correctly kept out of this diff — it is a different instrument with a different blast radius, and grading it is triage's.

Proceeding to the merge queue.

## Armed — auto-merge `SQUASH`, and the probe I will run afterwards, written first

Armed at **2026-09-11T16:34:20Z** on head `cfdc50f1627b835e66da2667ef5f209bae4c8797`. ⓘ The arm call echoed `method: MERGE`; ⛔ that echo is not the authority — `origin/main` is linear and a prior PR's branch commit is not an ancestor of it, so the queue squashes. One commit will land.

### The probe, written and posted BEFORE the merge

Every expected value was read off `cfdc50f162` **just now**. Post-merge legs are scoped to `<merge>^ <merge>` — ⛔ never to `origin/main`, which moves. Tree reads only: ⛔ no runner leg, because this seat has a bare checkout and a leg it cannot run is indistinguishable from one that passed.

**L1 — the file set, two-sided.** `git diff --name-only <merge>^ <merge>` = exactly **2** paths: `scripts/check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs` and `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-expression-carriage.test.ts`. A third path is a FAIL.

**L2 — nothing moved in transit, by blob**, paired with a count and a string:

| path | expected blob |
|:--|:--|
| `scripts/check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs` | `cf846c5576cce36170b378eda307cc48fc758941` |
| `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-expression-carriage.test.ts` | `83e5b6f4e30e2ab17871eeb3f791658e3d1d50fe` |

⭐ Cross-check that costs nothing: `cf846c55…` is the **same** blob prefix the PR body quotes as the pre-mutation baseline in both ablation legs. The report's ablation and my read of the tree are describing one object.

Count: **+394 / −24** across the two files. String: the line below, which is L3's subject.

**L3 — the fence that must STAY, which is the leg I would reject over.** Triage's binding fence is ⛔ *do not widen the census*. Two readings, both on the merge commit:

```
export const JSON_FENCE_LANGUAGES = ['json', 'jsonc'];
```

byte-identical to `<merge>^` — ⛔ `plaintext` never enters — **and** `parseFenceDialect(` occurs at exactly **3** non-comment sites: its own `export function`, the blind-spot leg, and the in-run control. The blind-spot site must sit **between** `if (!fence.scanned) {` and that branch's `continue`, so the judged path cannot reach it. ⛔ A count alone would not prove that; the leg reads the enclosing branch.

**L4 — the report-only posture, the other thing that must STAY.** Lines matching `process.exit|exitCode`: **6** at `<merge>^`, **6** at `<merge>` — ⛔ EQUAL. A report-only gate that starts exiting 1 on 26 reported fences would redden `Build Docs` for every page in the corpus, and that would be this change turning blocking through the back door.

**L5 — the retired pin is gone and its replacement is present, each with a control that hits in its own half.** ⛔ An absence claim alone is worth nothing, so both halves are positive somewhere:

| anchor | `<merge>^` | `<merge>` |
|:--|--:|--:|
| test title `measures the DIALECT blind spot instead of asserting there is none` | **1** | **0** |
| test title `SEES the JS object-literal dialect the coverage line used to lie about` | **0** | **1** |
| `${DOCS_ROOT}/components/…` lines inside the per-file floor | 0 | **5** — ⛔ per file, not one total |
| `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(5)` | 0 | **1** |

⚠️ **A correction to my own probe, made by dry-running it rather than by posting it.** My first spelling of L5 asserted that `unscannedJsonLike).toEqual([])` is absent on the merge commit. It read **1** on the head and **0** on the base — the exact inverse of what the leg claimed, and a leg whose control does not fire. Printing the matched lines explained both halves: the head's hit is the new docblock *quoting* the retired pin, and the base's assertion is the two-argument `expect(value, message).toEqual([])` spread over ten lines, which a single-line grep cannot see. ⇒ the anchors above are **test titles**, single strings, extracted from the source on both sides. ⛔ The PR body's paraphrase `expect(census.unscannedJsonLike).toEqual([])` is substantively right and is ⛔ not the literal text — which is exactly why a probe leg is written against the tree and never against a report's prose.

**What the probe does NOT claim.** It does not re-run the gate, the pins, the two ablation legs, or the byte-identical census diff — I cannot, and CI is the reading that covers those. It says nothing about whether 26 is the right number; the instrument decides that. A green probe is a statement about **what landed**, ⛔ never an endorsement of the class.

A leg that comes back amber will be published with its cause. ⛔ It will not be re-run into green.

## LANDED — `7696daac04e149124e733f879d4972fa40770215`

Merged as one squash commit. Probe run scoped to `7696daac04^ 7696daac04` (parent `729e851dc2`) — ⛔ never against `origin/main`, which has moved twice since. **All five legs green**, each against the value posted before the merge.

### L1 — the file set, two-sided ✅

```
scripts/__tests__/check-doc-expression-carriage.test.ts
scripts/check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs
```

Count **2**, and the set EQUALS the two named. No third path.

### L2 — nothing moved in transit ✅

| path | expected | on the merge commit |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `scripts/check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs` | `cf846c5576…` | ✅ `cf846c5576cce36170b378eda307cc48fc758941` |
| `…/__tests__/check-doc-expression-carriage.test.ts` | `83e5b6f4e3…` | ✅ `83e5b6f4e30e2ab17871eeb3f791658e3d1d50fe` |

Paired count: **394 insertions / 24 deletions** — exact.

### L3 — the fence that must STAY ✅, and one reading that needs saying out loud

```
export const JSON_FENCE_LANGUAGES = ['json', 'jsonc'];
```

Byte-identical across the merge. ⚠️ **It sits at line 233 on the parent and line 250 on the merge commit** — that is the mechanical consequence of 394 lines landing above it, ⛔ not a change. This is exactly why the leg was written to compare the **string** and not a `path:line`: a line-number diff here would have read as movement and been wrong.

`parseFenceDialect(` occurs at exactly **3** non-comment sites — its own `export function`, the blind-spot leg, the in-run control — and the blind-spot one is inside its branch:

```js
  for (const fence of scan.fences) {
    if (!fence.scanned) {
      const dialect = fence.ok ? 'json' : 'object-literal';
      const jsonLike = fence.ok ? fence : parseFenceDialect(fence.body.join('\n'));
      …
      continue;
    }
```

⇒ ⛔ the judged population cannot reach the normalizer. Triage's binding fence — *"do not fix this by widening the census"* — holds **structurally on the merged tree**, not by assertion.

### L4 — report-only posture ✅

`process.exit|exitCode` lines: **6** at `<merge>^`, **6** at `<merge>` — EQUAL. A gate now reporting 26 fences cannot redden `Build Docs` for the whole corpus.

### L5 — the pin swap, each half positive in its own ref ✅

| anchor | `<merge>^` | `<merge>` |
|:--|--:|--:|
| `measures the DIALECT blind spot instead of asserting there is none` | **1** | **0** |
| `SEES the JS object-literal dialect the coverage line used to lie about` | **0** | **1** |
| `${DOCS_ROOT}/components/` floor lines | 0 | **5** |
| `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(5)` | 0 | **1** |

Both directions positive somewhere, so neither half is an unfalsifiable absence. The pin that passed *because the leg it pinned was blind* is gone; a per-file floor with a non-vacuity floor stands in its place, and ⛔ no equality was pinned on the total.

### ⛔ What this green does NOT say

It says **what landed**. It does not re-run the gate, the pins, the two ablation legs, or the byte-identical census diff — this seat has a bare checkout and ⛔ writes no leg it cannot execute; CI's four green shards on this head are the reading that covers those.

And it is ⛔ not an endorsement of the class. The gate now reports **26** fences it cannot judge instead of printing `✅ Dialect blind spot: none` over them. ⭐ That is the whole deliverable: the coverage line is now **derived** rather than declared. A detector that reports full coverage precisely where it is blind is the worst shape one can take, and this one no longer takes it.

Closing objectui#8334.
